newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks surge to another record close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks surge to another record close.

text.p: Australian stocks limped through early trade on Thursday but recovered to reach full stride late in the day and end on their fifth record close in a week.
The All Ordinaries Index dropped immediately after opening but was later spurred on by banks and leading miner BHP to close 19.9 points up at 2,693.3.
"It was a weird sort of day, it started soft and surged at the end," said broker Robert Cameron of Cameron Securities.
BHP -- the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd -- was one of the star performers as shares in Australia's biggest listed company picked up 45 cents to close at A$19.72 (US$14,79) on volume of 5.8 million.
BHP surged after analysts said they had revised up their profit forecasts for the embattled blue chip which this week announced a strong rise in copper production.
"BHP is very solid," said Cameron, who added overseas buying had helped push the All Ordinaries almost 12 points higher than the previous record set on Tuesday.

The banking sector also contributed to the rise in the All Ordinaries, which had dropped sharply immediately after opening in the wake of a third successive dip on Wall Street and a slump in the gold price.
The banks index jumped 1.35 percent to finish on 4,829.2 as investors chased yield stocks.
All four major banks closed over 12 cents or more higher, ANZ up 25 cents to A$9.80 on 1.6 million shares traded.

National Australia Bank jumped 18 cents to A$18.83 on trade of 1.2 million shares, Commonwealth Bank was up 15 cents at A$15.20 and Westpac rose 12 cents to A$7.87 after 2.8 million shares were traded.

Nickel producer QNI Ltd had a mixed first day back on the bourse after Wednesday's announcement of its merger with South Africa's Gencor Ltd. Brokers said investors had still not digested all the details of the merger.
QNI shares ended three cents down at A$2.65 on volume of 9.2 million shares. (A$ = US$0.75)
